title: The role of exogenous ketone bodies in maintaining immune homeostasis in healthy subjects
summary:
When following a low-carbohydrate diet or during extended fasting periods, the body produces ketone bodies from fatty acids as an alternative energy source. These ketone bodies not only serve as energy carriers but also seem to play a role in maintaining health and immunological balance. The biochemical mechanisms behind this effect are currently being studied.
Although a ketogenic diet, which reduces carbohydrate intake to less than 10%, is safe and free from side effects, it requires significant changes in dietary habits that can be challenging to maintain in everyday life. As an alternative to this strict diet, exogenous ketone bodies have been available as dietary supplements for some time. These supplements can increase blood ketone levels without dietary changes and come in the form of ketone salts or ketone esters. Ketone salts are powders suitable for making ketone shakes and are often enriched with minerals like magnesium or calcium. Ketone esters are available in liquid form.
It remains unclear whether consuming these ketones, like a low-carbohydrate diet, contributes to health maintenance by stabilizing the human immune system. This study aims to investigate whether the intake of exogenous ketones as dietary supplements helps maintain health. This knowledge could lay the foundation for future studies and potentially provide new treatment approaches for certain health conditions.
conditions: This study aims to determine the extent to which the intake of exogenous ketones, potentially combined with a low-carbohydrate diet, contributes to maintaining health and immune homeostasis in healthy subjects.

Inclusion criteria:
